newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's MMT (St Petersburg) declares 96 dividends.
newsitem.headline: Russia's MMT (St Petersburg) declares 96 dividends.

text.p: Shareholders of St Petersburg's long distance phone company (MMT) approved 1996 dividends of 888.5 roubles for preferred shares and 88.5 roubles for ordinaries, both with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
Dividends for 1995, before a 10:1 stock split and revaluation, were 5,657 roubles for prefs with a nominal value of 16.67 roubles. Ordinaries of the same nominal value were not paid dividends.
AO Mezhdugorodny Mezhdunarodny Telefon (MMT) announced the following results, based on Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis, at its April 29 shareholders meeting:
Last year shareholders increased charter capital to 66.2 billion roubles from 110.4 million roubles based on revaluation.
Shares of MMT on the Russian Trading System had not traded on Tuesday after closing at $2.25 on April 22, the last day it traded. It's high and low for the year were $3.25 and $1.75.

NOTE These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
